question: Should OpenClaw add declarative `bindings[].match.content` with optional body stripping to core routing, or keep bindings static and route content-based dispatch through a plugin/pre-routing hook?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but the choice changes public config shape, routing precedence, cache semantics, plugin boundaries, and channel delivery behavior; automation cannot safely choose that product/API boundary.

options.title: Adopt Core Content Bindings
options.body: Add a validated binding matcher with explicit regex/prefix safety, deterministic precedence, route-cache treatment, body-rewrite semantics, docs, and representative channel tests.

options.title: Use Plugin Hook Instead
options.body: Keep core bindings static and treat content classification as plugin-owned once a bounded pre-routing hook is approved and documented.

options.title: Defer The Feature
options.body: Keep the middleman-agent workaround for now and revisit after the broader pre-routing hook and Discord routing decisions settle.

recommendation.title: Adopt Core Content Bindings
recommendation.body: Add a validated binding matcher with explicit regex/prefix safety, deterministic precedence, route-cache treatment, body-rewrite semantics, docs, and representative channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combination of original routing history and current issue-review context for this product/API boundary.
